newsitem.title: USA: Advocacy groups urge FDA to regulate cigars.
newsitem.headline: Advocacy groups urge FDA to regulate cigars.

text.p: Anti-smoking groups, citing a rise in teen-age cigar smoking, Thursday asked the Food and Drug Administration to regulate cigars the same way it regulates cigarettes and smokeless tobacco.
Nine organizations filed a complaint with the FDA similar to the one filed several years ago that led to the historic drive to regulate nicotine as a drug.

When the FDA first starting looking at regulating nicotine, it concentrated on smokeless tobacco and cigarettes as "drug delivery devices." It did not stress pipes and cigars, largely because young people did not use them much.

But cigars have since become a new fad which, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control, is attracting teens. The CDC recently reported that more than one of four high school students -- and one in three high school males -- smoked all or part of a cigar in the last year.

The health groups, including the American College of Chest Physicians and Action on Smoking and Health (ASH), argued in their complaint that the FDA must take on cigars because of their use by youngsters.

"Their use by young people is at least comparable to their use of smokeless tobacco products, and the health risks from such use are at least as great as those from smokeless tobacco products," ASH said in a statement.

Most of the controversy about tobacco regulation is focused on cigarettes and smokeless tobaccos. Pipes and cigars were not central to the $368 billion agreement reached last week by tobacco companies and the state officials suing them.
